# goldbot — status and next steps

Canonical design: `docs/DESIGN.md` (exported from the original Claude design doc; edit it here from now on).
Standing instructions for Claude sessions: `CLAUDE.md`. Owner's VPS guide: `docs/RUNBOOK.md`.

## Where things are (as of 2026-10-05)
- 2026-11-12 (branch fix/downtime-bars-catch-up; backlog 161, R126): base closes missed while the engine is down now
  count toward open trades' holds (engine/downtime.py). Each open trade saves `bars_through`, the last base close in
  its `bars_held`, in the same orders-file record; at the first base close after a restart it is credited the closes
  in between whose base bar had a minute in `SessionTable.expected_open` (the engine's session table less exchange
  holidays, the history gap guard's calendar: weekends, the daily break and holidays never count). Its time exit fires
  at that close; an exit-policy hard flat fires there (also above the floor) only when its policy timeframe's close at
  or after the deadline fell inside the downtime, else at that
  policy close, as before. Before, the hold ran long by the
  downtime. Credits are logged per trade and kept in `downtime_bars` (orders file and closed-trade record):
  time_exit/hard_flat with downtime_bars>0 exits at the restart close, not the label deadline: excluded from
  label-vs-live exit-price/slippage reconciliation. Closed trades before this deploy that were open during engine
  downtime held past their pre-registered hold and are flagged in performance reads, not pooled silently. The dead-feed
  time barrier now counts from `bars_through`, so a feed dying right after a restart no longer re-counts closes in
  `bars_held` (an early exit). Shadow trades open across a restart are tagged `restart_gap` (backlog 165 replays
  them). Follow-ups: backlog 163 (a re-closed bar re-runs its entries), 164 (no-quote barrier's any-minute rule).
  A close at or before `bars_through` is never counted again (a restart whose first quote is stamped before a counted
  close). Exits only get earlier. Not changed: the first deploy's own downtime is not credited (old files have no
  `bars_through`); closes skipped while running (a failed positions read, a bar no tick fell in) are not credited; a
  stale re-closed bar still runs its decisions, as before (only its count is skipped; backlog 163).
  Replay golden unchanged; store golden: restart.json only (`bars_through: null`, `downtime_bars: 0` on each in-memory
  open trade).
  Tests: tests/test_engine_downtime_catch_up.py.
- 2026-11-12 (branch fix/history-reread-off-tick; backlog 157, 159; R127): the engine's store reads after the warm
  start no longer run on the tick thread. The history re-read (while `history_read` / `history_short` refuses entries)
  and the release reload (while a window has a hole) each run on a thread of their own, one of each at a time, and
  the tick thread merges a finished read at its next bar close; a hung store delays no tick and no exit. The refusal
  holds until a read has finished, merged and been judged (`history_short` re-judged as before); a read that never
  returns keeps entries refused and logs one error after 120 s ("has not returned"). Release minutes are merged only
  before the cut-over current at the merge; a re-read never lifts a failure stamped after it started, and a read thread that dies without a result fails closed. Behaviour change: a re-read or reload is merged at the first close after it returns, usually one close after it
  starts (it used to merge at the close that started it). Key zones: an unreadable store cache now warns once per exception type
  with its traceback, then at most hourly with the count of that type, and logs "cache readable again" once on recovery. Owner
  step when the hung-read error fires: check the data root's disk and the store lock; the engine keeps trading
  exits. Tests: tests/test_engine_history_read.py (backlog 157 section), tests/test_engine_key_zones.py (backlog 159).
- 2026-11-12 (branch fix/pass-budget-log-noise; R134): the engine's "pass budget ... spent after N of N books" line
  no longer warns every minute when every book ran and only 15m+ work was carried (now DEBUG). The WARNING fires once
  per run of passes that left books out; the run's first clean pass logs one INFO "pass budget run ended after K
  passes over S s; L with books left out, most 15m+ parts carried C". Metrics (`passes_deferred`), the carry and the
  zones' deferred flag are unchanged. To see carried-only passes on the brain, raise goldbot.engine to DEBUG.
- 2026-11-12 (branch fix/restart-gap-other-shadow-reads; backlog 174, R132): the last shadow-book readers follow the
  R129 rule for `restart_gap` trades (statistics leave them out; risk guards keep their losses, drop their wins).
  Auto-mode evidence (`automode.match_outcomes`) leaves them out, win or loss, and says how many in its reasons; the performance report counts the
  proposal unmatched with "shadow path incomplete across a restart (restart_gap)", out of its R, money and
  calibration; the ruin estimate (`ruin.r_from_shadow_book`) keeps a gap loss and drops a gap win, counted and noted in the report. Finding on the
  exploration 1m/5m minute pass: its last decided minute was memory-only, so a restart inside that minute decided it
  again and a signal refused there could pass at a later price (reproduced in the test). Fixed: on the host clock an
  engine start counts every complete minute as decided, with or without an orders file (`exploration.start_minute`,
  journalled `exploration_start_minute`);
  at most one minute's signals are lost per restart. Replays on the tick clock are unchanged.
- 2026-11-12 (branch fix/restart-rerun-barrier-shadow; backlogs 163, 164, 165, R129): three restart follow-ups of
  backlog 161. (163) The last processed base close is saved per book with the orders file (`closed_through`) before
  that close's decisions run, and restored at start (journalled `restart_closed_through`): a restart whose first
  quote is stamped before it treats the quote as a late tick and never closes or decides that bar again, so an entry
  RiskGate refused at the original close cannot pass at a later price. The exploration step starts at the restored
  close too. A proposal pending at the restart is archived at start and journalled `restart_archived` there (before,
  the row came only from re-deciding its close); its card expires at once and its id is never raised again; a saved close ahead of the host clock plus one bar is ignored (journalled). A trade without
  `bars_through` keeps counting its dead-feed barrier from its entry bar until this engine processes a close. Old
  files start as before. (164) The dead-feed time barrier counts a bar when any of its minutes is
  expected open (`downtime.open_bars`, the catch-up's rule): the bar the daily break ends inside counts, a CME holiday
  does not. (165) Shadow trades open across a restart are held at start and replayed through the bars missed while
  down once the history covers them: no fill running or unabsorbed and not one expected-open minute missing
  (`engine/shadow_replay.py`, point in time, identical to never restarting); not covered within 6 h, or no resume
  point (`last_bar_ts`, new on each shadow trade): `restart_gap`, now left out of promotion stats, shadow_z,
  recalibration and the throttle's shadow win; the 12% re-arm read and the CUSUM model watch keep gap losses and drop
  only gap wins (trading-safety: an alarm must never lose a loss). Not changed: the exploration 1m/5m minute pass (its own per-minute state) and
  the perf/automode/ruin shadow reads still count `restart_gap` trades (backlog 174). Replay and store goldens unchanged. runner.py LINE_CAP 3083 -> 3073.
  Tests: tests/test_engine_restart_rerun.py, tests/test_engine_no_quote_barrier.py, tests/test_shadow_restart_replay.py.
- 2026-11-12 (branch fix/store-order-quarantine-journal; backlog 158, 162, R128): three data-layer fixes.
  (1) Quarantine spans fail closed: a failing read of dq_events or a quarantine table raises
  `quarantine.QuarantineReadError` instead of "no spans". Callers: D12 `reconcile_account` raises and the
  feed_reconcile job reports it (no report graded without the spans); `record_span` writes nothing; the nightly
  learner returns `evidence_exclusions:QuarantineReadError` and does not run; the nightly cost job counts the
  scheduled probes with none held out (safety S-1: probes only ever raise a slippage cell, so the cost can only be
  overstated, never dropped to the prior; note in the table); the daily review records an `unreadable` incident; the labs n holds every candidate of
  the account out (n understated, H-61 stop unchanged); scripts/evidence_exclusions.py exits with the error. A missing
  table or a schema without the span columns is still no spans.
  (2) `Store.read` orders by ts_utc, then the table's KEY_COLUMNS, then every column except year/month: ties
  (positioning series on one date, dq_events in one minute, multi-source bars) read in one content order, run after
  run, on duckdb 1.5.6 and 2.0.0. Column names are quoted (`check` failed before), scan paths escape quotes.
  macro.first_release, macro.merge_vintages, positioning.merge_releases and positioning_local's GLD check use stable
  sorts. Known effect (quant Q-C2): ticks sharing a ts_utc now read sorted by bid then ask, not arrival order, so the
  D12 engine minute built from stored ticks opens at the lowest and closes at the highest tied bid (at most one tick,
  data-quality grading only; live bars are built in memory). Code review measured 2M bars_1m rows 0.49 -> 0.51 s. Read time, a year of 1m bars
  (377k rows): 2.0.0 +5 % (0.129 -> 0.135 s), 1.5.6 +9 % (0.140 -> 0.152 s), medians of 25 on a loaded Mac.
  (3) The health pass's decisions-journal read (history_gap / order_failed) scans only the account's own
  source=/symbol= folder from the read's month (`Store.read(folder_only=True)`), with the four columns it uses cast
  explicitly, so a folder whose parts are all-null in a column types it as the whole table does. Synthetic journal,
  9,447 parts over 3 accounts: 0.58 -> 0.11 s on 2.0.0, 0.52 -> 0.11 s on 1.5.6, frames equal. A cast column no part
  of the folder has falls back to the whole-table read. Journal compaction is filed as backlog 170 (not done here).
  Labs n holds the accounts out on any failure of the span read, not only QuarantineReadError (quant Q-C3).
  Behaviour a reader could notice: any consumer that relied on the old tie order now sees the content order; a
  corrupt part in another account's journal no longer breaks this account's health read.
- 2026-11-11 (branch fix/cold-start-trade-ageing; backlog 160, R124): open trades age from every base bar close after
  any cold start. Before, `on_bar_close` returned at its 400-bar floor before `_manage_open`, so after a restart with no
  stored history an open trade's `bars_held` paused until the first decision frame (~30 h for 15m arms) and its time
  exit fired that late (broker SL/TP and tick stops still ran). Now the time exit fires at its bar; `bars_held` is
  saved in the orders file, so a restart resumes the count (bars missed while the engine was down are still not
  counted: backlog 161). Below the floor a policy's hard flat also fires at the first base close at or after its
  deadline (review C1) and the orders file is saved at that close (C2); the trail still waits for its frame
  (engine/below_floor.py). The replay golden was regenerated:
  the replay starts cold, so 6 RB15 trades of 2025-03-03 now time out after 4 bars instead of riding to stop/target;
  the freed slots move 7 entries in on 03-03; 11 RB15 entries of 03-04 go (`arm_budget`: the arm's daily loss room)
  and 5 later ones go (`min_lot_exceeds_risk`: lower equity). Ledger legs of trades opened in a no-history cold start
  before R124 may show stop/target where the arm's hold was a time exit; the performance-analyst ledger-vs-label
  reconciliation excludes or flags them.
  Tests: tests/test_engine_cold_start_ageing.py.
- 2026-11-11 (branch feat/duckdb-2-ready; backlog 156, R125): the Parquet store runs on duckdb 2. On 2.0 every
  ts-filtered `Store.read` raised a BinderException (a pandas datetime64[ns, UTC] column reads as TIMESTAMPTZ_NS),
  which the engine's history and the cross-feed reconcile turned into empty reads (49 test failures, all from that one
  filter; backlog 155 already made the engine fail closed on it). The bounds are now ISO strings duckdb casts to the
  column's own type, so they stay in the Parquet scan (2.0 EXPLAIN ANALYZE: 1-2 of 20/80 row groups scanned) and pick
  the same rows on both majors. `Store.read` and `Store.sql` return every zoned column tz-aware UTC at microsecond
  resolution (2.x returned it naive, 1.x in the host's zone: `Store.sql` on the Mac gave Europe/London), with the
  session zone pinned to UTC. duckdb is bounded `<3`, uv.lock pins 2.x, Dependabot tracks duckdb majors again. Deploy:
  the brain and VPS get 2.x on their next `uv sync --frozen`; the research/data workflows (`pip install -e .`) get the
  newest 2.x. Release files and the local positioning/dq_events store read identically (rows, dtypes) on 1.5.6 and 2.x.
  Found, not changed: `Store.read` orders by ts_utc only, so rows sharing a ts_utc come back in a different order run to
  run on either major (positioning, dq_events); backlog 162 proposes a deterministic tie order.
  Provenance (quant): the store library moves from duckdb 1.5.6 to 2.0.0 (uv.lock); windows, labels, costs and K are
  unchanged; tests/test_store_duckdb_compat.py pins a tick 1 ns outside either bound as excluded on both majors.
  Deploy checks (trading-safety): `uv pip show duckdb` = 2.0.0 on the brain; first warm start loads >= warm_start_min_bars
  with no history_read/history_short refusal or BinderException; no data_quality_error for ~15 min; key zones and
  blackouts load; reconcile coverage passes. Rollback: revert uv.lock to 1.5.6 and `uv sync --frozen` (no data migration).
- Deploy offer works again under the telegram sandbox (R120, incident docs/incidents/2026-11-10-deploy-check-exit-255.md):
  `DeployWatch.check()` no longer runs `git fetch`. Under ProtectSystem=strict that could not write /opt/goldbot/.git
  and exited 255 on every pass, so no version was ever offered. The check now reads origin main with `git ls-remote`
  (30 s timeout, no credential prompt) and asks GitHub's compare API for the fast-forward, the commit subjects (newest
  15, each cut to 120 chars) and the MT5-box ancestry. GitHub answers are streamed and capped at 5 MB and 30 s; 5 MB
  rather than 2 MB because a compare carries the patches. If git or GitHub fails, nothing is offered and one warning
  is logged per outage, with no traceback. Each successful read goes to state/deploy/check.json. The new health check
  `deploy_read` warns and tells the owner after 2 h without one (RUNBOOK 0.5 "No new version offered"). Deploys
  themselves are unchanged (`sudo goldbot-deploy`).
  **Post-deploy host check (brain):**
  `sudo systemd-run --uid=goldbot -p ProtectSystem=strict -p ReadWritePaths=/opt/goldbot/state --wait --pipe -d /opt/goldbot /opt/goldbot/.venv/bin/python -m goldbot.ops.deploy check`
  must print JSON or `null` with no warning. An offer it prints is recorded as pending, so Telegram does not repeat it.
  The incident closes once this check passes.
- 2026-11-10 (branch fix/fast-arms-first; R118; vantage-demo refusals diagnosis 2026-11-10 fixes 2-4): 1m/5m
  exploration arms now go ahead of the 15m+ close work. Each book's exploration pass runs its 1m/5m part (reads,
  the minute's decisions, a send) before its learning read and 15m+ step; a multi-book pass runs every book's 1m/5m
  part first and the 15m+ parts after (`books._slow_parts`), starting none while a 1m/5m signal is queued or a minute
  is due or inside its 1.5 s grace (max wait SLOW_WAIT_S 20 s; past the 5 s budget the rest are carried, first next
  pass). Fake-clock test, 11 books x 3 s step at a :15 close: S0 ages at send 6.2-38.2 s (9-10 of 11 stale) before,
  3.0-6.9 s (0 stale) after; last 15m+ step starts at ~41 s (60 s limit). Only the order changes: refusals, RiskGate,
  budget reads, PER_PASS per book and journal rows unchanged. The deferral warning shows exploration sub-phases
  `[reads, learning, step, minutes, entry, budget]` and the carried count. Not changed: gold's own bar close still
  runs before the other books' 1m parts; per-book step CPU is not reduced (next: optimise the top sub-phase).
  Review round 1: the learning read also runs before the 1m/5m send when a learning-group signal of any timeframe
  is queued (quant C1); a delayed 15m+ send re-reads its book's quote (held to a later pass if unreadable or faulty),
  and an order that raised on any book in the pass holds every later 15m+ send (trading-safety 5, 6); a quiet book
  leaves the carry. Tested: under a permanent 1m backlog every book's 15m close is still stepped before the next
  close (SLOW_WAIT_S). Watch items (quant C2, trading-safety 7): blocked-reason and take-rate reviews split by
  timeframe and by deploy date (pre/post R118); report the 15m split-pair rate against its pre-R118 baseline; after
  deploy, count 15m `exploration_stale` refusals on vantage-demo (expected ~0; any rise is the 15m+ part waiting too
  long behind 1m work).
- Health pass cost, second step (R121, after #360): the Telegram service's 60 s health pass no longer re-parses config
  YAML or re-reads an unchanged decisions journal. `goldbot.config.safe_load_cached` parses a file once per version
  ((inode, mtime_ns, size), as `_registry_rows`) and hands each caller its own copy; `load_arms`, `load_accounts` and
  the strategy catalogue use it. `history_gap:<account>` re-reads the journal only when a part file was added and
  otherwise filters its last read to the window: same verdict as a fresh read, a new refusal is seen on the next pass.
  The `session_local` DST-gap refusal is memoised per (zone, minute). Local warm pass (repo state, no engine files)
  4.58 s -> 0.28 s; a synthetic 4,500-part journal for three accounts reads in 0.93 s cold, 5 ms unchanged. Still to
  measure on the brain after deploy: pass < 5 s in the journal, service < 5 % of a core over 1 h. Not addressed:
  the journal read after each flush still costs the full DuckDB scan (thousands of one-flush part files; compacting
  `decisions` is a data-engineer item), and `read_learning_closes` (pnl_basis) rebuilds the trade ledger every pass.
- Health pass cost, third step (R122, after #364; brain round 3: warm pass 7-8 s, service 13 % of a core). Every
  verdict and research result unchanged. phase_gates: `director._Ledger` matches trials to ad-hoc pre-registrations
  through `_AdhocIndex` (by `ts`, same pick as the old linear scan, which `tests/test_director_adhoc_index.py` keeps as
  the oracle), and `evaluate_gates` counts `n_trials_effective` once (it was built twice per evaluation). Synthetic
  5,930 + 5,930 rows: 2.68 s -> 0.05 s. order_failed reads the decisions journal through history_gap's part-file
  cache, both from the earlier of their windows (`_journal_from`), so one read per flush serves both; data_quality
  reads dq_events again only when the table's part set changes (`_cached_window` in checks/_base.py). pnl_basis: the
  trade ledger resolves the instruments registry once per build and re-selects aux.db's exploration records only
  when aux.db or aux.db-wal changed ((inode, mtime_ns, size) equal before and after the read and older than
  `AUX_RACY_S` = 2 s; `PRAGMA data_version` is per connection and so no use to a reader that opens its own). Still
  to measure on the brain after deploy: pass < 5 s across a :00/:15/:30/:45 flush, service < 5 % of a core over 1 h.
  Not addressed: Store.read still scans every part of the table after a flush (data-engineer item).
- 2026-11-10 (branch fix/history-read-fails-closed; backlog 155, R123): a store read of the engine's history fails
  closed. Before, a raising read at warm start crashed the engine service (open trades unmanaged until a restart
  that crashed again), and the key zones kept a failed cache read for good (history_days 52.4). Now the engine starts,
  runs its exits, and refuses every entry while the read fails (`history_read`: RiskGate data_quality_error, specialist
  closes journalled `history_read:<tf>`, engine health FAILs naming it); the store is re-read every 30 min of engine
  clock and lifts it only once its minutes merged, then judges the window for `history_short` (review round 1: a
  recovered read no longer opens entries on a short window). A weekday-gold warm start with fewer than
  `engine.warm_start_min_bars` (28 800, capped at the 90 000 bars kept) 1m bars refuses the same way
  (`history_short:<tf>`) until the window holds them. After a failed or short read, open trades' time exits below the 400-bar floor now
  run at their close. Each re-read's duration is logged (warning over 2 s). Follow-ups: backlog 157 (re-read off the
  tick thread), 158 (quarantine spans read fails closed), 159 (key-zones warning throttle). Owner step when it fires:
  check the data root syncs (the health reason names the cause). Tests: tests/test_engine_history_read.py.
- 2026-11-10 (branch fix/swap-mode-5-6; Vantage refusals 2026-11-10 item 2, fix 1): vantage-demo BTCUSD reports MT5
  swap mode 5 (interest on the current price, 360-day year), which instruments.db stored NULL, so every BTC entry was
  refused `invalid:swap_usd_per_oz` (95 in 7 days). `instruments_db.swap_per_lot` now converts modes 5 and 6 to
  rate / 100 / 360 x price x contract size per lot per night (broker sign kept; an entry's open price is the current
  one); no finite price > 0 leaves it unknown, modes 7/8 stay unknown. `books.refresh_terms` takes the tick the

  The swap is fixed at the refresh price for up to `broker_terms_every_s` (6 h): a projection input, not a fill.
  RiskGate unchanged. Tests: `tests/test_instruments_db.py`.
- Quant review (b): mode 5/6 is priced only for a USD profit currency (the engine's SwapSpec reads the amount as USD);
  any other stays `swap_unknown`, the reason in `swap_note`. Follow-ups: BACKLOG 153 (seven-night crypto rollovers;

- After deploy (vantage-demo): check the live BTCUSD `swap_rollover3days` is in 1..5 (else `refresh_terms` keeps

- 2026-11-10 (branch fix/telegram-clean-shutdown; follow-up to R119): the telegram service stops cleanly. The pump
  was started with `app.create_task` in post_init and never cancelled, so every stop logged "Task was destroyed but
  it is pending!" (journal 15:25:34 UTC). `post_shutdown` now cancels and awaits the pump (at most HEALTH_STOP_S)
  before the audit drain, so nothing is written after the drain, then stops a running health pass as before. No
  change to proposals, the 90 s confirm window, exits or the outbox. Tests: tests/test_telegram_health_task.py
  (`test_shutdown_cancels_the_pump_so_no_task_is_left_pending`, `test_shutdown_works_for_a_bot_whose_pump_never_started`).
- 2026-11-10 (branch fix/telegram-health-cpu; telegram CPU attribution 2026-11-10, R119): the telegram service's
  health pass no longer holds the pump. `_pump` starts it as its own task (`_start_health_pass`), one at a time (a
  pass due while the last still runs is skipped and logged), so proposal cards and outcome edits keep flowing every
  poll; each pass logs `health pass s=<seconds>` and warns over `HEALTH_SLOW_S` (20 s). Review fixes: an exception
  escaping the task is logged at once (done-callback); run_checks still running after `HEALTH_HANG_S` (240 s) is
  logged as an error and then awaited, never abandoned (no second worker thread); shutdown cancels and awaits the
  task (`HEALTH_STOP_S`). The pass's two hot spots are
  gone: `arms._registry_rows` parses `state/research_registry.jsonl` once per file version (inode, mtime_ns, size;
  234 reads of a 3,353-row copy 7.3 s -> 0.35 s), and `registry.stale_preregistrations` indexes withdrawals and trial
  reads once (`_Exemptions`; same answer as the old scan, n_trials_effective warm 1.15 s -> 0.12 s on that copy, more
  on the brain's 778-withdrawal registry). No health check decides differently. Not done: the strategy catalogue

- 2026-11-09 trading-safety R1/R2 (branch fix/account-recheck-1109): **the terminal's account is checked again after
  start** (`goldbot/engine/terminal_account.py`). The service wires the start check (`accounts.verify_terminal_account`,
  `services.engine.verify_account`) into `Engine.verify_account`; it runs on every account refresh and every
  reconciliation. On a mismatch: entries refused `terminal_account_changed` (RiskGate), the account read is not used
  (equity, stages, high-water mark, risk period keep this account's last reading), every positions and deals read is
  refused and counted as `positions_unreadable` (no adoption, no inferred close, no unconfirmed-order resolution from
  the other book), engine state `terminal_account_changed` (health `engine:<account>` FAIL) and one Telegram notice each
  way. Exits are never gated; positions keep their broker stops. Back on the account, entries resume after
  `healthy_resume_s`. **R2:** an exploration or cost-probe ledger row settled by the BACKLOG 72 look-up carries
  `resolution` (`adopted` / `opened_closed` / `unfilled`; JSON body only, no migration); the retcode stays as answered.
  Golden `tests/data/engine_store_golden` regenerated for the new engine-state key only.
  Review round 1 (trading-safety 2 HIGH, 2 MED, 4 LOW): the risk-period roll checks its own read and rolls only once the
  terminal is back; exits are never gated while flagged (due closes, the engine stop and the kill switch send by ticket,
  never dropped as gone, never re-reading the whole account); `no_quote_pass` checks every `reconcile_every_s` and the
  kill switch checks before a whole-account read; a re-arm waits unconsumed (`rearm_refused` terminal_account_changed;
  re-arm source pin in tests/test_demo_roll.py updated); a closed record takes the engine's equity; `note_resolution`
  opens the ledger inside its try; every book's `data_recovering` waits `healthy_resume_s` from the restore.
  Residual-risk ruling: while a flagged read names another trade server than the one the account was last verified on

- **EVAL-2 Lane 1, twins (R107, quant approved 2026-11-09).** `goldbot/research/catalogue/sim.py` draws up to 20
  replay-only twins per signal from decision bars after its exit (intraday 7 days, 1d 20 bars), same side and hour

  - Cause: `on_bar_close` computed the family weights (regime, features) before the timeframe loop, so an exception there skipped `_manage_policies` (time exits, exit policies) for every timeframe and `_blackout_close` (pre-news exits); one raised by `_decide` skipped the later timeframes' policies the same way. Broker-side SL/TP still protected open trades.

- Health alerts and the outside dead man's switch no longer flap (owner 2026-11-04: "the health checks have been horrible ... up and down"; the emails came from the switch). Branch `fix/health-alert-flapping`:
  - Hysteresis (goldbot/ops/health.py `step_alerts`, `AlertPolicy`; settings `telegram.alert_confirm_polls` 3, `alert_confirm_min` 5, `alert_flap_note` 3): a check is told failing, and told recovered, only once the change held on 3 consecutive health passes AND for 5 min. A failure that clears inside the window sends nothing. The immediate list alerts on the first pass (`IMMEDIATE_NAMES`: kill_switch:, daily_cap:, weekly_cap:, order_failed:, backup_age, backup_prune, object_storage, bridge:, heartbeat:, engine:, engine_loop:; `IMMEDIATE_REASONS`: CRITICAL, terminal AutoTrading off, terminal on another account). bridge:, heartbeat:, engine: and engine_loop: are on it because each already waits before it fails: 5 min, 5 min, 45 min and 150 s. With engine_loop: on the list (SRE review MEDIUM), a dead or hung engine alerts in about 3 min. A check that failed and cleared inside the window 3 times in an hour gets one "flapping (not alerted)" line, at most hourly. Several changes still go out as one message.
  - state/health_last.json keeps `statuses` (the last report, still read by the deploy and daily-review checks) and adds `announced`, `pending` (kind, first_seen, polls), `flaps` and `flap_noted`. A file of the old shape loads with announced = statuses. `HealthWatch(state_dir)` without a policy keeps the old rule (every change at once) for the check-level tests; the Telegram service passes `AlertPolicy.from_settings`.
  - Dead man's switch (goldbot/ops/deadman.py): a daemon liveness thread (`start_liveness`) beats every min(60 s, half of `deadman_every_min`). It never waits on a health pass, so the monitor's period and grace no longer matter. It pings only on a health verdict: the first completed pass, or the last pass seeded from state/health_last.json when under 5 min old. Without one it sends nothing, so a service that crashes in every pass goes silent and the monitor turns down (SRE review HIGH). It keeps beating through a slow shutdown, so a deploy restart is not an email. The health pass only hands over its verdict (`observe`). `/fail` is sent for a confirmed failure (the same hysteresis or the immediate list), a Telegram alert undelivered on 2 passes in a row (SRE review LOW), or a verdict older than 5 min (`HEALTH_STALE_S`: a frozen pump, `health_checks_not_completing`). A transient FAIL pings ok and names the check in the body. `/start` is not used because it can only add emails. The owner has nothing to change on the monitor.
  - Alert log: aux.db migration 22 `health_alerts` (goldbot/ops/alert_log.py; ts_ns, channel telegram|deadman, kinds, checks) has one row per Telegram health message sent and one per state change the switch accepted (each change is one email). Count with `AlertLog(state).count_since(ts, channel=...)`.
  - Measured 2026-11-04 (no health or ping history existed before this change): there were 3 goldbot-telegram restarts (08:31, 10:59, 13:47; two hit the 90 s stop timeout). Under the old rule each left about 4.5 to 7 min without a ping (the last pass-driven ping plus stop, start and a first health pass of over 3 min before the CPU fix). That is up to 6 down/up emails against the RUNBOOK's 2 + 3 min. Under the new rule each gap is at most about 2 min (one beat plus the 33 to 56 s the process was really down), so 0 emails. Slow passes that made pings late: 0 under the new rule, but the old count is unknown. Transient FAILs: unknown, since nothing logged them; from now on aux.db health_alerts records them. Telegram: replaying today's tick-error timestamps gives 8 messages under the old rule and 7 under the new. tick_errors: holds each warning 15 min by design, so hysteresis barely touches it.
- engine:<account> stays FAIL after a one-off tick error (2026-11-04: one BridgeUnavailable blip at 06:27:56 UTC on all three accounts kept `engine:<account>` at FAIL for 12+ min while the engines passed every minute):
  - Cause: the engine's entry block is right (it clears only when a whole clean decision bar closes, up to ~30 min on 15m bars, exits never gated), but health FAILed for as long as `tick_error` was set.
  - Fix: the engine publishes `tick_error_since` (first error of the current block, host clock; kept on a repeat, cleared with the block). `engine:<account>` now FAILs only while the error is current: one in the last 120 s (`TICK_ERROR_CURRENT_S`), or a block older than 2 decision periods + 5 min (`TICK_ERROR_STUCK_S`, 35 min, pinned to `EngineConfig.decision_tf` by a test) with the market open throughout (errors repeating). Otherwise WARN with the age ("tick error (BridgeUnavailable) 12 min ago"). An engine without `tick_error_since` falls back to `last_tick_error_at`; one without either FAILs as before. The entry block itself is unchanged; `tick_errors:<account>` still WARNs on each error.

- **Multi-book pass under its budget (2026-11-04; live demo issue, icm-probe: "pass budget 5.0 s spent after
  8|16|19 of 20 books").** Measured first with `scripts/bench_account_pass.py`. It runs icm-probe's 20 books and
  registered arms on a paper terminal with 60 days of synthetic 1m history, one `account_pass` a second, counts every
  bridge call and has optional `--latency-ms` and `--profile`. Bridge calls are not the cost: about one `ticks_many`
  a pass. CPU is: the 15m close's pass took 11.3 s on the first close after a start and 4.2 s warm (Mac). Changes:
  1. `Frame.X` (new `engine/frames.py`) builds the features on first read. Only agents, the shadow book and blackout
     re-scores read them, so the 19 non-gold books (no agents) no longer build them. The regime is computed only on a
     book with agents (its only reader).
  2. `IncrementalResampler` compares datetime columns as epoch ns. Before, it built a Python Timestamp for every row
     of `visible_at` on every call.
  3. `history.window_gaps` keeps each hole's answer in a per-book `GapMemo`. Before, every close of every book
     re-judged the same weekend holes minute by minute. A new session table, covered span or limit clears the memo.
  4. `mid()` builds its frame in one go.
  After (same harness): 15m close 1.9 s cold and 0.64 s warm; minute passes 190 ms against 202 ms. The budget,
  `PASS_BUDGET_S` = 5 s, is unchanged. Key zones are left as they are: one build per 15m close on gold only, on its
  own thread, 0.11-0.16 s on 800 days of 15m bars here. The brain's logged 1.6-1.8 s suggests the brain runs about
  10x slower than this Mac, so warm 15m closes should now take about 6 s there instead of about 40 s.
  Decisions are bit-identical: `tests/test_pass_budget.py` runs a 33-minute, 3-book session with icm-probe's arms
  and real entries twice, through these fast paths and through reference copies of the old code. Every journal row,
  deal, position, gap and queued signal must match. `tests/test_perf_equivalence.py` covers the resampler and `mid`.
  One behaviour change, on the error path only: a feature build that raises no longer fails the bar close of a book
  without agents, because that book never builds the features. A book with agents fails as before.
  Not done:
  - The 1m S0 rule (`arm_rules.random_bracket`) scores its whole lookback every minute, though the engine takes only
    the last bar. This is about 5 ms a book a minute on the Mac and is the next lever; it needs quant review.
  - Not measured on the brain itself.
  Review: trading-safety (bar-close path: lazy features, regime only with agents).
- **icm-probe stale entries and the vantage-demo close-retry storm (2026-11-04).** Both measured on the brain
  (read-only: py-spy 0.4.3 run from /tmp, /proc schedstat, the journal and the decision parquet; nothing written on
  the server, the temp files removed).
  1. **Brain CPU starvation.** The brain has 2 cores. The api and telegram services each used a full core: 96-97%
     of their py-spy samples were in `instruments_view._registry`, which parsed config/instruments.yaml once per
     ledger row (`instrument_key`). CPU pressure (PSI "some") was 46%. icm-probe's main thread waited 1.83 s on
     the run queue for every 1 s it ran (345 s run against 631 s waiting since its 11:00 start). This, not the
     engine, is the main reason "the brain is 10x slower than the Mac", and it explains why db07bff7 did not help
     there. Fix: the registry is parsed once per version of the file (mtime and size). An edit is read on the next
     call, and an unreadable file is logged once per version.
  2. **Engine pass (150 s py-spy of icm-probe across the 11:59 and 12:00 closes).** 147 passes: median 0.34 s, p90
     1.66 s, max 10.5 s. Within passes: bridge round trips 62.9 s, everything else 59.9 s, of which about 2/3 was
     waiting for CPU. Main bridge costs: `ticks_many` about 166 ms a pass, `account` and `account_positions` about
     50 ms each, and `loss_per_lot` 8.9 s in total. Fixes: `PassBroker` asks `loss_per_lot` once a pass for each
     exact question. Every book's exploration pass used to ask again for the same open positions' loss at their
     stops. The deferred-pass warning now gives the exits time and the three slowest books with their seconds, so
     the next measurement needs no profiler.
  3. **Why entries go stale.** It is not tick age. `exploration._enter` measures a signal's age from its bar close.
     453 of today's stale refusals were S0-* (the 1m random control on all 19 non-gold books, firing in the same
     minute) plus LCS5A/B, with a median age of 18.6 s against a 10 s limit. A 1m decision waits for the broker's
     M1 bar, which arrives 3.7-5 s after the close. The first order of a minute goes out a median 7.3 s after the
     close, and later orders follow every 2.7 s (median). Each order runs serially through place_order, last_tick,
     a full `_refresh_account` (account, positions, deals_since, exposure) and two orders-file writes. A fresh tick
     would not help, and the limit is unchanged.
     Model on the measured split: removing the run-queue wait cuts pass time by about a third (in-pass 123 s to
     about 82 s per 150 s). At 20 books, p90 goes from about 1.7 s to about 1.1 s; at 26 books (the owner's list),
     about 1.4 s. In a minute's S0 sweep, roughly 4-5 orders fit inside 10 s instead of about 2. Stale refusals
     should fall (LCS5A/B on gold, which runs first, should mostly clear) but will not reach zero: 19 S0 signals
     in the same minute cannot be sent serially within 10 s at about 1.5-2.7 s an order. Next levers (not done,
     order path, need trading-safety review): a lighter account re-read after an exploration fill, and orders-file
     writes once a pass.
  4. **vantage-demo close storm.** The probes had closed on their own stop or target. `_retry_closes` dropped the
     due close of a position the broker no longer listed, and the 30 s hold timer (`cost_probe.hold_exits`) sent
     it again on the next pass, until the bar close's sweep 14.5 min later. New `engine/close_retry.py`:
     - A gone position is recorded at once from its exit deal (`broker_close`, journalled `close_due_gone`). With no
       deal yet it is kept due, without sending a close, for the sweep.
     - A close refused while the position is still open keeps being sent: every 1 s for 30 refusals, then backed
       off, doubling, with one warning per try. The cap is 5 s, except for a scheduled exit (probe or arm hold,
       time exit) whose price is still short of the engine's stop, which gets 30 s. So kill, Friday cut, hard
       flat and engine-stop closes are never more than 5 s apart (trading-safety review MEDIUM).
     - The refusal count is kept apart from the market-closed backoff count, and a market-closed refusal resets
       it. `gone()` keeps its own look count.
     - A missing instruments.yaml is cached as missing, so it is not re-read or logged on every call.
     A paper replay of the incident sent 560 closes before and 1 after. Exploration hold exits skip due closes, so
     they are covered too.
  Not done: the effect on the brain is modelled, not observed (needs a deploy). The serial order path still caps a
  minute's sends. The S0 sweep's design (19 books in the same minute) is a quant question.

- Growth test: GS1's pyramid adds, the part of growth sprint section 3 that was deferred (a logged deviation, due
  11-03). GS1C gets the same adds. Registered as `adds: 3` on both arms in config/accounts.yaml (growth-sized arms
  only). An add goes out at each +1 R from the first unit's entry, R being the stop distance the gate set on that
  unit. Each add is a signal like any other: every engine bound, then the RiskGate. An add is sized at most at the
  first unit's lots and takes its group's arm and pot slot. Before an add is sent, every earlier stop moves to the
  newest add's 1 R stop, so the group never loses more than one unit. This rule is tighter than the C2 screen's
  common stop: ADR 0065 gives the reason and asks for quant review. A refused add's level is spent and recorded as a
  blocked candidate (a shadow fill). Every pass, whatever the entry state, a group above one unit has its earlier
  stops moved back. After a restart the groups are adopted from the deterministic add ids and the ladder resumes.
  Each add carries `group_id`. Also fixed: every growth-pot candidate had been quarantined as an unknown style since
  PR #257, so the nightly replay never scored it and no shadow fill existed. Rows written from 11-01 up to the
  deploy are released once by `scripts/unquarantine_growth_obs_2026_11_02.py` (RUNBOOK, icm-demo learning host).
  Review round 1 (PR #266). Safety: the add path confirms every earlier stop at the broker before the add goes out
  (a rejected or raising modify refuses it), and the group stop check runs first in the pass in its own try. Quant
  (growth sprint Â§3, protocol deviation 2): ADR 0065 is accepted. Units are 0.01 lots (`unit_lots`), so both legs'
  8 units fit the 0.10 net lots. A pyramid unit has no profit target, and a group exits together at its stop or its
  end. The read (perf-report, health, `scripts/growth_sprint_read.py`) never counts a refused add as a trade: it is

- Autonomous discovery phase 2 (ADR 0058): the honesty set, generator G2 and the `autodisc_nightly` job. `autodisc/stats.py` holds pure functions with known-case tests: White RC and Hansen SPA (consistent version) on a stationary bootstrap, batch PBO (CSCV), deflated Sharpe at the ledger K with each spec's own skew and kurtosis, a circular-shift null, and a plateau check (at least 60% of neighbours positive and a neighbour mean of at least 0.5 x the peak). `autodisc/gen_gp.py` is typed GP over the leaves `PrimitiveProvider` computes, with structure and time leaves weighted 2:1 over regime. It uses NSGA-II selection on fitness, complexity and turnover, is bounded at population x (generations + 1) evaluations and is deterministic under its seed. Every evaluated candidate is ledgered before its result. Its G0 null reruns the whole search on random sides and counts in K_null. `autodisc/nightly.py` runs the search, the null and the honesty set, then writes `state/autodisc/survivors-<day>.md` (counts use thousands separators, so no 2018+ number can appear) and a health line. Grid neighbours are ledgered and counted in K. The job is off unless `research.autodisc.nightly_enabled`, because ADR 0058 section 5 keeps all search off the brain. On the Mac it runs with `python scripts/autodisc.py nightly`. It creates no arm and imports nothing that trades. Also fixed: the phase 1 CLI report raised whenever a count fell in 2018-2099. Not built: ONC K_eff (the DSR uses raw K_search, which is conservative) and novelty labels for G2 survivors. Review round (2026-10-30, quant and code findings in one pass): the circular-shift null now moves the signal by whole weeks in calendar time (whole days under 40 weeks of sample) and scores excess R over the drift baseline, so an hour or session drift no longer beats it; the G2 fitness is the min-fold t of that excess R (gold's drift is not skill against the driftless G0 null). The report states the cumulative K_search and the cumulative survivor count over all nights (a survivors table in the ledger), each survivor's DSR at the cumulative K against the 0.95 confirm bar, and one line per judged candidate that failed with its failed check. ADR 0058 carries a dated pre-registered amendment: advancing to confirm needs DSR >= 0.95 at the cumulative K_search, the plateau ratio, the K_eff deferral and the variance caveat. The registry link (decision 2, k_contrib) is a phase-3 precondition with a strict xfail test, because design 3.1 keeps independent hypotheses at the registry's K and an unknown row status would read as a trial on an older host. Also fixed: a measured cost table's build date no longer fails the report, a raw dir without 2010-2017 files skips the night, the report is written atomically, and the GP tournament never exceeds the population. Measured on the 3,000-bar synthetic tensor: the excess-R fitness recovers a 0.4 R injected edge less often than net R did (1 of 6 seeds against 3 of 6), because the drift baseline there rests on about 125 bars per (hour, side) cell; the power test now injects 0.6 R. Re-review owed: quant (F1-F5 as applied) and code.
- Autonomous discovery phase 3 (ADR 0058, amendment 2026-10-30 phase 3): confirm and holdout. `goldbot/research/autodisc/confirm.py`: `preregister_confirm` (refused unless the spec is a recorded explore survivor with DSR >= 0.95 at the cumulative K_search on 200+ events and an explore t; one ad-hoc registry pre-registration, `rule_ref autodisc:<hash>`, frozen reading rule and explore numbers, at most 8 a month in one monthly batch), `run_confirm_batch` (the month's batch read once on 2018-01 .. 2025-09 under the registry lock: budget via `check_budget_reserved`, Holm at 5% over the batch, DSR at the registry's `n_trials_discovery` + the batch, the gates' positive years, 1.5x cost stress, the explore 90% prediction interval; one `autodisc_confirm` trial row and its verdict row each) and `holdout_read` (a confirm passer with a "continue" verdict, once, `gates.holdout_verdict`, never a `holdout_contaminated` spec). Every read is journalled before it looks in a hash-chained `stage_reads` table beside the search ledger (`autodisc/stages.py`, unique per stage and hash, so a hash is never re-read; a crashed read is closed void, charged and stopped). The read is rule-only on the outcome tensor (same evaluator and cost model as explore); a pass is never `passed_gates`, so promotion and live are unchanged. Real reader: `confirm.stage_backends` (1m bars plus a year of warm-up, cut at the stage end on load; `windows.StageFrame` refuses any later bar). CLI `scripts/autodisc.py confirm-prereg | confirm-run --batch YYYY-MM | holdout`. F3: `TrialRegistry.record_discovery_batch` / `n_trials_discovery` (registry K + every batch's k_contrib) in a sidecar `<registry>.discovery.jsonl`, so `n_trials_effective`, `is_trial`, the budget and registry_sync never see a batch (an older host cannot count one); `autodisc/k_link.sync_discovery_k` tops it up to the ledger's K_search after every real night and before every confirm step (the strict xfail is now a passing test). `autodisc-register` now takes only confirm or holdout passers by default (journalled `stage`), explore survivors only with `--stage explore` (journalled `requested_stage`), and never a spec whose confirm or holdout read failed or was voided; its default ledger is now `state/discovery_real.db` (the nightly's). From the first real nightly runs: every ledgered result carries `search_fitness` and its components (fold t, excess fold t, t_stat, time in market, floor failures); specs that beat the null but failed an explore check are listed in the survivors report with the check and its value; `nightly --timeframe 15m|1h|4h`. Mac scheduling: `scripts/install_autodisc_launchd.sh` (dry run; `--apply`) installs `com.goldbot.autodisc` (01:30 local) running `scripts/autodisc_nightly_mac.sh` (15m, 1h, 4h in turn, logs `~/tmp/autodisc`, refuses off the Mac); RUNBOOK "Autonomous discovery on the Mac". Not run: no real confirm or holdout read (each is a one-time look and needs an open budget slot; 2026Q4 has none), the launchd agent is not installed. Review round 1 (trading-safety safe; quant F1-F4 applied): grammar v1 K 864 counted and the explore DSR read at the registry discovery K; survivor DSR re-read from stored inputs at the day's K; measured cost table required to advance and for every stage read (no priors fallback), explore net mean R > 0; holdout also needs the session-day clustered t >= 1.65; an absent ledger is refused; tests that 2025-10+ bars leave the confirm read unchanged and that stage passes never count for promotion; RUNBOOK notes the Mac runs whatever branch is checked out.
- Autonomous discovery phase 4 (ADR 0058, design section 4.1-4.2): demo arms from discovered specs. `goldbot/research/arm_rules_spec.py` is the one interpreter (`RULE_FUNCS["spec_rule"]`): it runs a ledger spec bar by bar through the explore evaluator's own primitives (`LiveProvider` is `PrimitiveProvider` without the explore cut), so a G1 spec's live entry bars, side and ATR stop equal the research masks (tests on a golden synthetic set, a trailing-window warm-up test and a no-lookahead perturbation). It places no order and starts nothing. Reviews owed: trading-safety (engine arm selection, config load) and quant (interpreter parity, the registration's survivor rule). Review round 1: a bad row in `config/spec_arms.yaml` is dropped and journalled (`exploration_arm_dropped`), never a startup crash (only the live-class refusal stays fatal); `check` also refuses a family leaf whose arm needs stored bars or replica state and any spec the engine cannot warm up; `autodisc-register` is idempotent (rerun after a crash replays the file edits from the journalled row, no new row or weekly slot), recounts the weekly cap and duplicates inside the journal transaction under a file lock, refuses on main or a detached HEAD (rows go through PR + CI), rounds the cap to pence, hashes every journal column, and `--verify [--head <digest>]` detects a deleted tail.

(exploration 1,300, control 20, probes 158)"); still WARN-only, an unreadable aux.db is a WARN with the reason. Its row carries `excess_r` (mean net R less the control's mean net R, matched by risk day x session x side with the control weighted by the family's cell mix; trades in a cell without control trades are dropped and counted) and a Welch 90% interval on the difference only when both sides have 30+ trades; the verdict is "above / below / not distinguishable from the random control", and no learning row reads "mean R above zero". Root cause: the 1m/5m exploration pass (`exploration._minutes`) built the minute that had just closed from the engine's sampled quotes. That minute's `tick_count` was the number of distinct quotes polled (at most four a second at the 0.25 s loop). The 60 minutes before it came from the broker's M1 bars, whose `tick_count` is MT5 `tick_volume`. So v_t was compared with the median of a different feed and never reached 2.5 x it. This broke H-81 section 0 ("compared with its own trailing median on the same feed"). The broker's bars do carry tick volume: `mt5_adapter` renames `tick_volume` to `tick_count`, and `history.rates_to_bars` keeps it. Fix: with broker bars on, every minute whose broker bar has been fetched is the broker's (`broker_bars.fetched`, laid over the sampled minutes). The minute just closed also waits for its bar, as a decision close does (`broker_bars.awaiting`, now shared with `hold`: at most 3 s past close + 1.5 s, while no finished call covered it). The rule and its thresholds are unchanged. The same fix applies to the other volume rules (Z2P's v_t < v_{t-2}, Z8P, Z5P) and to the 1m/5m arms' spread gate. Past the hold the minute is decided on the sampled bar, as the engine's own closes are. Reviews owed: trading-safety (the minute pass's 3 s wait is on the entry path; exits do not wait) and quant (live now matches the backtest's volume definition).
- Exploration arms stop by their pre-registered rule, now data in `config/arm_stops.yaml` (`goldbot/research/arm_stops.py`; evaluator's spec/code mismatch 2026-10-27). W1 families (arms-expansion 2.1) stop on their POOLED running net R at -30 R within 300 fills; W2 (arms 8.0) the same or on futility at 300 (one-sided 95% UB of mean net R < +0.03 R, SE clustered by UTC day); Z/H-81 families pool across strata and brokers, futility read on >= 20 session days; F1A/G1A keep H-61's stop plus their futility reads, and F1C/G1C stop only with them. H-61 arms (BXR* included) keep the per-style stop; controls never stop. Before this, every arm stopped by its style, so e.g. a 15m W1 arm was retired at -15 R within 100 instead of its family's -30 R within 300. H-81 cost stop per stratum: at >= 30 fills a 95% UB of signal-time cost/R above 0.10 halves the stratum's share live (engine `shares`), above 0.20 the daily review retires it under the cost rule. A stop only refuses new entries (`exploration_arm_status`, unchanged path); no exit is touched. Review round 1 (quant and trading-safety): futility weights strata equally (mean of stratum means, SE from stacked fills clustered by day); a stopped family retires every member on every broker reviewed, fills or not (Z3V/Z5V before V2), and F1C/G1C with it; WFRI's 26-Friday safety check (mean net <= -20 bp or cumulative <= -10 R) runs beside H-61's swing stop; a suspended stratum is refused before any room check (no first-trade bypass, `cost_suspended`); a broken or missing arm_stops.yaml refuses exploration entries as `stop_rules_unreadable`. Reviews owed: quant-reviewer (rule reading, futility/CR1, pooling), trading-safety-reviewer (engine share scaling, retirement path).
- BACKLOG 135, MT5 bridge close priority (ADR 0056, protocol v7). The bridge now accepts requests concurrently and runs each terminal connection's calls on one worker from a priority queue: closes and stop changes first, then /health, reads, and entry orders last; a request whose client went is never run, a read queued past its client's timeout (`timeout_s`, sent by the brain from v7) is dropped, an order queued past 10 s is refused stale. Opt-in per account (`order_lane: true` in config/accounts.yaml, off everywhere today): an order lane, a child process of the bridge with its own terminal connection that sends entries only, so ticks, closes, the Friday cut and the kill switch keep flowing while the terminal sends one (tests show < 5 s with an entry held 35 s). A lane that dies with an order gives no reply (ambiguous, settled by the BACKLOG 72 look-up, never re-sent) and stays down. A live account refuses entries on a bridge below v7; demo stays at MIN_COMPATIBLE 5, so either box can be deployed first. Deploy steps and the lane drill: RUNBOOK "Order lane (BACKLOG 135)". Unverified: two IPC clients on one MT5 terminal under Wine (the drill checks it before any account turns the lane on). Reviews owed: trading-safety-reviewer, sre, security-reviewer, code-reviewer.
- BACKLOG 135 review fixes (trading-safety on 49335812, ADR 0056 amendment 1): a live account takes entries only with bridge v7 and its order lane up (`separate`); a lane `down` FAILs health on any account; cancelled requests no longer fill the queue, and closes and stop changes are never refused by its cap; an order the lane never sent is a definite reject (`order_lane_not_sent`), not ambiguous; `load_accounts` now reads `order_lane`; `icm-live` gets `order_lane: true` and `terminal_path: C:\MT5\ICMarkets\terminal64.exe`. The pilot therefore needs the lane drill on the live box (this overrides bridge-v7-rollout.md section 8).
- Engine 1m close lag fixed: completed 1m bars now come from the broker's own M1 bars (`goldbot/engine/broker_bars.py`, D28). They are fetched with the existing `get_bars` once each minute closes. The call runs on its own thread with its own bridge client (one attempt, 2 s timeout), and failed calls back off exponentially up to 60 s, so the tick thread never waits on the bridge (trading-safety HIGH on c77be48d). A decision close waits at most 3 s past close + 1.5 s for its last minute's bar. Only entries wait: the close's time exits and account refresh (stage machine, kill switch, Friday cut) run when the hold starts. Broker bars that are unsound (NaN, high below low, bid above ask, or flagged by `bar_errors` as a replacement) are refused with `broker_bar_refused`. Through the bridge only: a terminal on the same host keeps the sampled bars. The bars built from sampled quotes are now used only for the current minute and as a fallback when the broker's bar is late or missing. A fallback minute gets a `broker_bar_late` dq warning, which does not block entries, and is replaced when the broker's bar arrives within 10 min (`broker_bar_replaced`). Decisions already taken stay as journalled. A bar joins only after it was fetched at or after its close, and visible_at is unchanged. Engine state now has a `broker_bars_1m` field with counts; the store golden was regenerated for that key only. This is on in production (bridge or terminal) and off for paper, replays and backtests. No bridge change was needed; `get_bars_range` (v6) is not used. Trading-safety review owed. After deploy, check that the D12 reconcile's closes-off count falls from about 83 a day.

A `place_order` that does not answer (the bridge's read timeout or a lost connection) is now an ambiguous order, looked up at the broker by its comment (BACKLOG 72: adopted, or not placed after two clean looks 120 s apart), never a tick error, so entries wait only until the look-up settles it instead of a whole decision bar. Through the bridge, entries go out on a worker thread with a client of their own and the account's new `order_timeout_s` (accounts.yaml; vantage-demo 35 s, default 15 s, at most 60 s); the tick thread waits at most 5 s for the reply (was up to 15 s), then carries on with its passes. A late reply is journalled `order_late` and brings the look-up forward to that pass. One order in flight per account (a second is refused before its row is written). A tick read that times out behind our own order in flight is not a tick error. Known limit (trading-safety MEDIUM): the MT5 box serves one call at a time, so engine-side closes do not keep per-tick cadence while an order is in flight; worst exit delay `exit_delay_bound_s`, about 45-55 s at 35 s (not a regression), covered by the broker-side stop; BACKLOG 135 fixes it before any real-money account. - Evidence exclusions (prereg Amendment 4, quant ruling 2026-10-26, blind). Two append-only aux.db tables (migration 19): `evidence_reloads` holds C (corrected bars visible) and R (the account's first engine warm start at or after C, never before) per account and span; `evidence_exclusions` lists the void order ids. Criterion v1: an exploration candidate or trade is void when decided at or after the span's start and before R, or when labelled before C from a label path overlapping the span. There is no lookback term: indicators are recomputed from the stored bars at every decision. A scheduled cost probe entered inside a span is void for the cost cells only. Readers that leave void rows out: the nightly posterior, the H-62 models and their retrain counts; the n toward the 300 read; the cost table's probe fills; the daily review's refit cells. Readers that keep them: the H-61 stops, P&L and broker reconciliation. The daily review prints a void-count line. Nothing is voided until R is recorded. Meanwhile the nightly learner, the arms' n (labs) and the cost table hold the span's decisions out in memory, together with any label path crossing it, and its probes; the daily review raises an ALERT line. The learner skips the night if it cannot screen the evidence. On the brain after deploy: `scripts/evidence_exclusions.py --corrected 2026-10-26T15:07:59Z --reloaded icm-demo=2026-10-26T15:09:35Z --reloaded icm-probe=2026-10-26T15:09:35Z` (dry run), then the same with `--apply`.

- Exploration first-trade rule: "first" is now by trades, not P&L. An arm whose trade closed today (flat or in profit, so its netted realised loss is 0) and that has nothing open is no longer fresh: its share of the pot governs again. Before, such an arm traded at its per-trade cap on every bar. A trade opened yesterday and closed today counts as today's (its loss is in today's figure).
- Exploration keeps one host slot for the scheduled cost probe in code (`exploration.probe_slot`, ADR 0043 "one of 18 kept for the scheduled probe"). With scheduled probes on, an arm is refused `probe_slot` (and the pass's other signals recorded blocked with that reason) when its entry would leave no free slot under the RiskGate's max_positions. Every open position counts except an open scheduled probe: exploration, mirror probes and foreign positions on the symbol. Before, only `max_open_total` (exploration positions alone) stood for the reserve, so mirror probes could take the last slot. With the shipped configs (icm-probe 12 scalp + 3 mirrors + 1) it does not bind today. No cap raised. Order path change: for trading-safety review.
- Exploration: a position closed at the broker (its stop or target) is swept at every reconciliation (`reconcile_every_s`, 30 s of tick time) once its exit deal is seen (`exploration.sweep`, called from `Engine._reconcile`), so its arm, pot and host slots and its open risk are free for the next signal. Before, they were held until the next decision-bar close, which kept 1m/5m arms from re-entering. A close with no exit deal yet, or unreadable deals, is still confirmed by the bar-close sweep. Order/exit path change: for trading-safety review.

- I2 `goldbot/risk/hwm.py`: a deposit or withdrawal (MT5 DEAL_BALANCE in the deal history) is a capital flow, never a rise: `capital_flows` + `apply_flows` move the mark by the net flow (a loss before a deposit is not forgiven; a withdrawal lowers it by exactly the amount), confirmed by the deal history only and only when the history since the mark's anchor reconciles with the balance (a flow the mark already holds is never counted twice: that would be a phantom drawdown and a 12% kill switch). Then the ADR 0018 rule gives max(mark + flow, balance). `HwmConfirmation.flows` (additive, default 0) keeps the explanation exact.
- I3 `goldbot/engine/runner.py` `_apply_capital_flows`: a flow stamped after the day's (week's) roll moves `day_start_equity` (`week_start_equity`) by the same amount at once, so the daily %, £ and weekly caps keep the loss so far mid-session (before, a £10k top-up read as profit until the roll). Journal `capital_flow` (kind, amount, shifts; no identifier); the risk file gains `week_reset` and `flows_through` (older files: the day roll and the mark's anchor; golden regenerated, only the two null keys added). The finance ledger already records the same balance operations (goldbot/ops/ledger.py RC-9). Residual: a deal clock skewed past a roll can shift a start that already holds the flow (a tightening: entries blocked, never a kill switch).
- ADR 0042 trading-safety review fixes (14f154aa): an older risk file anchors the capital-flow read at the week/day roll (not the mark's anchor), so a deposit the previous release folded into the mark at its restart still moves the starts (HIGH); a balance deal at or after a cancelled deal (MT5 13/14, ledger `follows_cancel`) is never a capital flow; a withdrawal lowers the starts only when the deal history reconciles it, and on any account that is not demo it lowers neither the mark nor the starts (tighten-only, it reads as a loss).

- Engine restart with the market closed blocked entries with `dq_error duplicate_ts` (brain 2026-10-25 08:05, icm-demo and icm-probe). Not DST: the terminal's frozen quote was Friday's last tick (2026-10-23 20:56:59 UTC = 23:56:59 EEST, converted correctly). The previous engine had finalised and stored minute 20:56. The restarted engine loaded it in warm_start, re-built the same minute from the re-delivered tick at the clock-driven close, and `_check_new_bars` saw the stamp twice. The same happens on any restart while the market is closed or quiet. Fix: warm_start records `Engine._history_through` (the last loaded `visible_at`), and a tick stamped before it never goes into the live bar builder, because its minute is already in the history. The block used to clear by itself only at the first decision-bar close after the reopen (~15 min of entries refused). Tests: `tests/test_engine_history_gap.py` (fall-back Sunday and a plain Saturday, plus new minutes are still built and a real duplicate still blocks).

- PUBLISHED SIGNATURES for L2 (replace the earlier `record_obs`, which is gone):
  `record_candidate(db, *, candidate_id, account_id, arm_id, family, style, tf, side, decision_utc, stop_dist, target_dist, max_hold_s, taken, is_control=False, arm_config_hash=None, blocked_reason=None, branch=None, u=None, mu=None, tau_arm=None, pi_rand_arm=None, meta_p=None, model_version=None, bandit_version=None, feature_version=None, feature_list_id=None, features=None, available_utc_max=None, snapshot_ref=None) -> bool`: at EVERY candidate's decision, taken or not (blocked: mu 0 + reason, branch "blocked"). `decision_utc` = the decision bar's close; `stop_dist`/`target_dist` the arm's own barriers in USD/oz, `max_hold_s` its time limit; `features` = the snapshot as computed at the decision (exactly the style's `FEATURE_LISTS[...]` columns) with `available_utc_max` <= decision. First record stands; invalid input (style, timeframe outside 1m/5m/15m/1h/4h/1d, side, barriers, mu/u outside [0,1], taken with mu 0, snapshot missing columns, availability after the decision) is kept quarantined, logged, never trained on.
  `record_fill(db, *, candidate_id, entry_utc, exit_utc, entry_price, exit_price, cost_per_oz, censored) -> bool`: a taken candidate's broker fill and close (candidate_id = the order's client order id); `label_fill_r` is a diagnostic only. `cost_per_oz` = commission + paid swap per oz (the spread is in the fill prices).
  `weights(db, arms, *, ceilings=None, now=None) -> dict[str, float]`: ONE style's strategy arms (no controls); each share of the style's budget in [0.05, min(0.30, ceiling)]. Equal shares in the same bounds when missing, stale (3 days), incomplete, mixed-style, out of bounds or unreadable.
- Label (training target): `label_sim_r`, a 1m bid/ask bar replay of every candidate (entry at the first 1m open at or after the decision at ask/bid; barriers minute by minute, stop first in a shared minute, a gap through the stop fills at the open, a target never better than the target; time exit at the first minute at or after the limit). Spread paid once through bid/ask, slippage max(0.15, measured) per leg never credited, commission, paid swap per rollover (a swap credit is not counted). `label_mid_r` = the same replay on mid with no cost (gross diagnostic). Cost model point in time (refused when effective after the cutoff), version recorded per row; unresolved labels stay NULL (excluded, never censored); written once. Bars: each account's own 1m bid/ask (`bars_1m`, source = account).
- `training_table(db, *, style, as_of, features=None, arm_id=None, feature_cols=None)`: the style's admissible rows (resolved by `as_of`, not quarantined, no holdout 2025-10-01..2026-09-30 decision), frozen v1 columns from the snapshot; rows without one (history, tests) join through `asof_join` with available_utc <= decision (spec rule B); the row invariant fails the build; `check_feature_cap` on the columns + side + arm_id. The v1 lists (38 per style, `f-079deacc61`) are in code once, and an integration test builds all three decision frames and finds every column at that feature version.

Retrain on Sundays when >= 1,500 new and >= 3,000 admissible labels; cutoff Friday 21:00 UTC, activation Sunday 22:00 UTC; saved as `state/models/h62/<style>/<version>.pkl` with its SHA-256 in `exploration_models`, registered with `status` 'shadow' (column default; 'shadow' | 'champion' | 'retired'). The units active before the deploy are recorded first; a failed restart no longer ends the start loop (it used to `return 1` at the first failure, so one engine whose bridge was not logged in left api, scheduler, telegram, news and tv-pull stopped through the rollback too). A rollback starts only those units, and after any rollback every one of them that is not active is started again; the record ends `running: ...; not running: ...`. A newly enabled engine (not active before) is started last with `--no-block` and judged on its own: down with a bridge check not ok (`bridge:`/`terminal:`/`bridge_compat:<account>`) is `deployed_degraded` "engine@<account> blocked by its bridge (<check>)", down with its bridge ok rolls back (and is not restarted by the rollback). An engine active before and down after still rolls back. Tests: tests/test_goldbot_deploy_sh.py (incident scenario, rollback restarts, watcher). RUNBOOK 0.5. **Install on the brain** with the hash-checked steps in RUNBOOK 0.5 "Installing a new goldbot-deploy".

- MT5 comment limit is 29 (incident 2026-10-20, icm-probe, MetaTrader5 5.0.6231 under Wine): `order_check` returned None with `(-2, 'Invalid "comment" argument')` for every scheduled cost probe, whose id `cm-sched-<epoch>-<10 hex>` is 30 characters; a probe of lengths 20..32 accepts 29 and refuses 30+. `goldbot/execution/broker.py` now has `MT5_COMMENT_MAX = 29` and `comment_keys(cid)` (whole id, last 29, legacy last 31). - **Adaptive risk limits, lane B: wired in** (ADR 0031). The nightly `limits_job` (scheduler, daily 23:05 UTC, never caught up past the roll; `goldbot/ops/limits_job.py`) decides each demo account with ceilings for the next risk day. Inputs: the FULL history of its demo fills (net R after the ADR 0017 imputed cost) and of taken shadow trades of versions that went live, since each version's `promoted_utc`, cut off before the decision day. A window would reset Amendment A1's 60-trade exploration count. Plus the engine file's drawdown and stage and the 15m ATR from the store. It persists through `AdaptiveController`, sends a dq_event (dq_events, source `adaptive_limits`) when evidence is missing or stale, and sends the owner an FYI on every change (masked account, no buttons). Health check `limits_controller:<account>` FAILs when the last decision is over 26 h old. The engine reads the decision through ADR 0032's seam (`engine/limits_apply.py` `AdaptiveLimitsController`). It takes the decision only at the 00:00 UTC roll, only tightens within a day (restarts too: seeded from the day's `limits_changes`), and gives the floors when the decision is not today's or the drawdown is 4%. `clamp` keeps it within [default .. ceiling], and the 8% revert gives the defaults. Live and tiny-live keep the defaults. The supervisor takes a lower published adaptive combined cap. Records carry `min_lot_exception`. `scripts/replay_limits.py` replays the record read-only (validates, never tunes; log each run in ADR 0031). Behaviour change: icm-demo now trades the floors (2% / 5%, minimum-lot cap 1.0% from the A1 exploration budget while the ATR rule allows) until the rules earn a loosening; `risk.adaptive_limits: false` restores ADR 0032's static ceilings. Gap: no 20-day cost/model series exists, so the cost rule is inert (BACKLOG 90).
- **Adaptive risk limits, lane A** (ADR 0031 with Amendment A1, rules frozen before any replay): `goldbot/risk/adaptive.py` computes the account daily/weekly caps, the supervisor caps and the minimum-lot cap from demo fills after each strategy's freeze. The statistic is a daily-R-sum LCB, and q is quarter-Kelly per strategy, the smaller of the trade and day terms, minimum over strategies. Loosening is demo-only, one step at the risk-day roll after 3 qualifying days and 10 new demo trades, never within 5 days of a tighten. Tightening is immediate (DD 4%, 4 losses at -0.8R, cost/model, size-down stage, weak statistic, shadow included). The demo minimum-lot cap starts with an exploration budget: 1.0% for the first 60 exception trades, off for good at -10R cumulative, paused by ATR, stage, cost, DD and the loss streak; then the LCB rule decides. Live accounts stay at the defaults; anything missing or corrupt gives the floors and a dq_event. State and an append-only change log live in core.db migration 4 (`adaptive_state`, `adaptive_changes`), after ADR 0032's migration 3. Not wired yet: lane B adapts it to ADR 0032's `LimitsController` seam.

- Parallel research trials, serialized registry record (`research.yml`, `goldbot/research/cells.py`). The workflow is now
  `plan` -> `trials` (matrix, `max-parallel: 10`, `contents: read` only) -> `record` (`concurrency: research-registry`,
  the only job that writes the registry or an issue). Inputs: the existing single-trial ones (one cell per variant, so
  `variants` now runs in parallel) and a new `batch` (JSON list of `{specialist, variants, pooled, timeframe, ...}`, a
  missing key takes the dispatch input; max 64 cells). Each cell fetches bars and a read-only registry snapshot, runs
  `research_pass.py` on a copy of it and uploads only the rows it added. `record` fetches the fresh registry under the
  lock, merges the rows (registry_sync's keyed union, idempotent on a re-run), restates every deflated Sharpe and the
  gate's DSR verdict on the FINAL `n_trials_effective` (`cells.restate_dsr`; the run's own value stays in
  `results.dsr_at_run`), saves by the usual compare-and-swap and posts one comment per `research: <family>` issue.
  - A cell's own report is provisional: its DSR and trial numbers use the snapshot count, not its siblings; the posted
    report says so and shows `at run -> restated on K`.
  - A cell that crashed, timed out or left no artifact records a `failed` trial row (counted in N, never passes a gate).
    A cell refused before any look (budget, queue, holdout rule; a message, no traceback) records nothing and is listed.
  - Known limit: each cell checks the quarter's budget on its snapshot, so a batch can overshoot it by up to its size;
    the report states the quarter's count after the record. Size a batch to the remaining budget.

- An approval whose send raises is archived NOT CONFIRMED, never left placing (BACKLOG 84, implementer, 2026-10-17;
  trading-safety residual on BACKLOG 72).
  - `ApprovalCenter._finish`: if `on_decision` raises, the card's `placing` flag is cleared and it is archived with
    the refusal code `not_confirmed` and the facts pending (as `unconfirmed.archive_pending` does), then the error is
    re-raised. A refusal or NOT CONFIRMED the engine already archived stands. The outbox reports it NOT CONFIRMED
    at once instead of after PLACING_MAX_S, and the dashboard no longer shows "submitted" and then drops it.
  - `engine/unconfirmed.py`: a `sending` row (the send raised, or the engine died mid-send and the outbox's
    silent-engine fallback reported the card NOT CONFIRMED) whose position is found later, by `_resolve_sent`
    (restart or stale-sending) or by the reconcile adopt, sends the "opened" notice once and rewrites the card.
    `_card` also rewrites a card still `placing` (`shown_unconfirmed`), which sets `not_confirmed`, the refusal code
    and clears `placing`. A `sending` row with no card shown NOT CONFIRMED (the auto path) is adopted silently, as
    before. No new owner-facing strings and no runner change.
  - Not covered: an engine silent for 60 s whose send then returns a plain fill (status `filled`, no look-up). The
    outbox has already reported NOT CONFIRMED, and no "opened" notice follows. A raise before the order row exists
    (for example `last_tick`) is also archived NOT CONFIRMED with nothing to look up, so the dashboard lists it as
    pending until UNCONFIRMED_LISTED_S. Both are routed to trading-safety.
- An approval that raises before its order row exists is archived "not sent", never "approved and sent" or NOT
  CONFIRMED (BACKLOG 85, implementer, 2026-10-17; trading-safety residual 1 on BACKLOG 84).
  - `Engine._on_decision` now wraps the old body (`_apply_decision`); on any raise it calls
    `unconfirmed.archive_not_sent`, then re-raises. With no `pending_orders` row for the proposal (nothing can have
    reached the broker) and no answer archived yet, the card gets the refusal code `not_sent:mt5_box` (a bridge error
    or a connection failure, e.g. `account()` at approval) or `not_sent:engine` (anything else), `placing` cleared,
    archived, one owner notice and a `not_sent` journal row. A raise after the row exists keeps BACKLOG 84 (NOT
    CONFIRMED, entries refused until the look-up settles it). No row, so nothing is pending and the next entry is
    allowed.
  - Wording in `goldbot/execution/not_placed.py` (`not_sent_code`, `NotPlaced.not_sent`, `by` gains "engine"): card
    "🛑 NOT PLACED: approved, but the order could not be sent: the MT5 box couldn't be reached. Nothing was sent.";
    dashboard red "Could not be sent. …; nothing was sent."; the notice names the trade and the masked account, never
    the proposal id, the exception, a host or a login. Rows added to docs/ux/order-not-placed.md for ui-ux approval.
  - API contract: `NotPlaced.by` gains "engine" and `NotPlaced.not_sent` (bool) is added; web/openapi.json and
    web/src/lib/schema.d.ts regenerated, `ProposalCard` picks the "Could not be sent" heading.
  - Trading-safety review LOW: only `BridgeError`, `ConnectionError` and `TimeoutError` read "the MT5 box couldn't be
    reached"; any other `OSError` (a local disk or file error) is `not_sent:engine`. The digest and the performance
    report count a not-sent card under "not placed by the MT5 box, the broker or the engine" (`CAUSE_PHRASE`).
- Broker tick record for the H-A holiday diagnostic (BACKLOG 79, data-engineer, 2026-10-17).
  - New daily scheduler job `tick_record`. For each enabled account it pulls the broker's XAUUSD ticks of closed
    server dates with `copy_ticks`, read-only, through the scheduler's existing broker connection (`_job_broker`,
    the one feed_reconcile and broker_ledger use). Each day goes to `state/ticks/<account>/<YYYY-MM-DD>.parquet`.
  - Trading-safety review (bridge load), fixed:
    - Two slots, 21:10 and 22:10 UTC, one in each DST regime's daily break, each with `max_late_hours` 0.5.
    - The job skips unless `market_quiet` holds (New York 17:05-17:50, or the weekend), and stops when the window
      ends.
    - Pages of 2000 rows with a 0.2 s pause. A page over 2 s or a run over 300 s stops the run; the unfinished day
      is not written.
    - One day per run, oldest first; the weekend runs catch up.
    - A test proves the job is read-only: its fake broker's order methods raise.
  - File contents: `time_ns` (int64, through `epoch_ns`), `bid`, `ask`, `flags`. Written atomically, mode 0600, in
    a 0700 directory. `index.json` records rows, London/NY ticks, median spread, bytes and sha256 per day.
  - Re-runs are idempotent. Missed days within `ticks.backfill_days` (7) are back-filled. Days older than
    `ticks.retain_days` are pruned.
  - Health `ticks:<account>` (WARN only) when the newest day has fewer than `ticks.min_london_ny_ticks` (1000)
    London/NY ticks, or has not advanced in 4 days.
  - Loader: `goldbot.data.ticks.load_day(account, day, state_dir=...)`, which verifies the sha256.
  - Size: about 12 B/tick, so 50k ticks is about 0.6 MB a day.
  - Backup: the files are backed up (the whole state dir is). The terminal's tick history is finite, so a lost day
    cannot be pulled again.
  - Deviation from the lane brief: no recorder in the engine and no change to runner.py.
    - The engine already stores its polled `last_tick` sample in `data/ticks/source=<account>`.
    - A polled sample misses ticks between reads, so it biases H-A's ticks-per-minute.
    - The pre-registration (docs/research/holiday-list-measurement-2026-10.md) fixes "copy_ticks after each server
      day closes, one Parquet per server date".
  - `retain_days` defaults to 240, not 90: H-A reads the 2026-11-26 file after 2027-04-30.
  - Not done:
    - the 90% uptime rule (terminal connection history);
    - compaction of the engine's per-minute `data/ticks` part files (about 1,400 files a day, existing debt).
